evidence.claim: Highway 11 began with a much different outline.
evidence.quote: State Highway 11 was authorized in 1920 from Donaldson east to International Falls, then south through the Iron Range to Duluth.

evidence.claim: Authorized in 1920, it ran from Donaldson east to International Falls, then south through the Iron Range to Duluth.
evidence.quote: State Highway 11 was authorized in 1920 from Donaldson east to International Falls, then south through the Iron Range to Duluth.

evidence.claim: In 1934, the north-south portion became US 53, while Highway 11 extended west to the Red River and east beyond Island View.
evidence.quote: In 1934, the north–south portion was redesignated U.S. 53, and Highway 11 was extended on the east to its current terminus east of Island View; and on the west to the Red River

evidence.claim: The final unpaved section, between the North Dakota line and Donaldson, was paved by 1961.
evidence.quote: The last section of Highway 11 to be paved was between the North Dakota state line and U.S. 75 at Donaldson; this was paved by 1961.

evidence.claim: For an eastbound journey, take Highway 11 from Karlstad toward Roseau and Warroad on Muskeg Bay.

evidence.claim: For an eastbound journey, take Highway 11 from Karlstad toward Roseau and Warroad on Muskeg Bay.

evidence.quote: Warroad is along the southwest shore of Lake of the Woods at Muskeg Bay, east of Roseau and west of Baudette.

evidence.claim: Warroad’s former railway depot is a brick replacement for a wooden station lost to fire in July 1914.
evidence.quote: A fire destroyed the wooden depot in July 1914, and it was rebuilt using brick.

evidence.claim: The original depot opened in 1900, when the town became a Canadian Northern Railway stop.
evidence.quote: In 1900, Warroad became a stop on the Canadian Northern Railway, and a depot opened in March.

evidence.claim: The replacement included customs and immigration offices, waiting space and living quarters for the stationmaster.
evidence.quote: included offices for customs, immigration, a baggage area, waiting room, and a stationmaster's quarters.

evidence.claim: Passenger service ended in 1977 and the station closed the next year.
evidence.quote: The last passenger train to stop at Warraod was in July 1977, and the station was closed in 1978.

evidence.claim: After renovation, the building housed city offices and a public library by July 1985.
evidence.quote: By July 1985, the station was used as city offices and a public library

evidence.claim: The town stands at Muskeg Bay, where commercial fishing gradually gave way to sport fishing and tourism.
evidence.quote: Warroad is along the southwest shore of Lake of the Woods at Muskeg Bay

evidence.claim: The town stands at Muskeg Bay, where commercial fishing gradually gave way to sport fishing and tourism.
evidence.quote: Warroad had a strong commercial fishing industry, which gradually turned to sport fishing and tourism.

evidence.claim: Zippel Bay State Park has a three-mile beach on Lake of the Woods, with white sand along the shoreline.
evidence.quote: ZippelBay State Park has a 3-mile long beach on Lake of the Woods.

evidence.claim: Zippel Bay State Park has a three-mile beach on Lake of the Woods, with white sand along the shoreline.
evidence.quote: It is on the white sand beach shoreline of the Lake of the Woods

evidence.claim: Wilhelm Zippel moved here in 1887 and built a home near the bay’s entrance.
evidence.quote: He moved to the area in 1887 and built a home on a peninsula near the entrance of Zippel Bay.

evidence.claim: His family established a commercial fishing business, and by 1909 a village included fishermen’s homes, a post office and cold storage.
evidence.quote: Zippel and his family established a commercial fishing enterprise on the lake. A small fishing village also was established in the area and was thriving by 1909. The village included a post office, cold-storage building and homes for the fishermen.

evidence.claim: Foundations, debris and depressions are the village’s remaining traces.
evidence.quote: There is little evidence of the remains of the village besides foundations, debris and depressions in the land.

evidence.claim: The state park was established in 1959 to provide public lake access; construction followed from 1963 to 1967.
evidence.quote: Zippel Bay State Park was established in 1959 to provide public access to Lake of the Woods and provide recreational opportunities in the area. Construction of the park did not get underway until 1963 and was completed in 1967.

evidence.claim: Lake of the Woods is a remnant of glacial Lake Agassiz, which once covered this part of Minnesota.
evidence.quote: Zippel Bay State Park is in a part of Minnesota that was at one time part of a glacial lake, Lake Agassiz. Lake of the Woods is a remnant of the glacial lake.

evidence.claim: White sand lines the Lake of the Woods shoreline.
evidence.quote: It is on the white sand beach shoreline of the Lake of the Woods

evidence.claim: The Rainy River was an escape route when fire largely destroyed Baudette in 1910.
evidence.quote: Baudette was largely destroyed in the Baudette Fire of 1910

evidence.claim: The Rainy River was an escape route when fire largely destroyed Baudette in 1910.
evidence.quote: Many of its people were saved by a train with boxcars sent across the river from Rainy River, Ontario

evidence.claim: A train sent from Rainy River, Ontario, carried many residents to safety across the water in boxcars.
evidence.quote: Many of its people were saved by a train with boxcars sent across the river from Rainy River, Ontario, which pulled survivors to safety on the other side.

evidence.claim: The town had developed as a steamboat landing and lumber community with a sawmill after the railway arrived in 1901.
evidence.quote: It was started by European Americans as a steamboat landing and lumber town with a sawmill, after the railroad was constructed through the area in 1901.

evidence.claim: It rebuilt quickly after the fire.
evidence.quote: Baudette was largely destroyed in the Baudette Fire of 1910, but was quickly rebuilt.

evidence.claim: Baudette lies where its namesake river meets the Rainy River, opposite the Ontario town that sent help.
evidence.quote: The city is along the Rainy River at its confluence with the Baudette River. It lies across the river from Rainy River, Ontario

evidence.claim: An international bridge connects the two communities.
evidence.quote: Baudette and Rainy River are connected by the Baudette–Rainy River International Bridge.
